0.long_answer: Tracheobronchomegaly, also known as Mounier-Kuhn syndrome, is characterized by the abnormal enlargement of the trachea and main bronchi. This condition involves a structural defect in the airway architecture, specifically manifesting as an anatomical deformity and loss of elastic fibers. As such, it is not primarily a problem with airway function or ventilation dynamics, but rather a physical abnormality of the airway structures. Therefore, tracheobronchomegaly is classified as a structural disorder.
